title: The same key twice, spelled the same way

source.note: composed: ECMA-404 does not say what a repeated name means, and this is the one case where the corpus's raw-text `input` is load-bearing — a case format that carried parsed JSON could not express it at all.

notes: Expectation: last occurrence wins, which is what every mainstream JSON parser does. serde_json and JSON.parse both resolve an exact repeat while building the object, so the protocol layer is handed one pair and never learns there were two; an implementation could only refuse it by writing its own JSON parser, which is a cost the corpus would be imposing on every implementation — the JavaScript one included — over a case ECMA-404 assigns no meaning to at all. Two *casings* of one name are a different matter and are refused (case 01): they survive parsing as distinct keys, and it is §5 that makes them one field with two values, which is the protocol's question rather than the parser's.
